narrative:
Based on the assessment, there is a 24% chance you will fail your final year. While this may not seem high, it exceeds the 10% threshold that triggers the requirement for remedial courses — a precautionary measure designed to support students before difficulties become serious.

The three factors that most influenced this prediction all actually worked in your favour, which is important context. The strongest positive signal came from your having no past class failures, which aligns perfectly with students who typically pass — this meaningfully reduced your predicted risk. Similarly, your father's educational background at secondary level, while slightly lower than the higher education level seen in roughly a quarter of non-obliged students, still contributed toward a passing prediction. Finally, your clear ambition to pursue higher education — a goal shared by every student in the non-obliged group — also pushed your prediction in a positive direction.

However, despite these reassuring factors, your overall risk profile across all the information considered still places you above the safety threshold. Notably, your very high levels of free time and going out with friends stand out compared to peers not required to take remedial courses, where such levels are rare. Your weekend alcohol consumption and school absences — averaging 8 compared to 2.8 among non-obliged students — also paint a picture of potential disengagement.

The remedial courses are not a punishment but an opportunity. You clearly have ambition and a solid foundation. The recommendation is to use this support to address any gaps, reduce absences, and channel your free time more productively toward your studies.
